policy.name: Government & Public Sector Document Classification and Reclassification Policy
policy.description: Governs class assignment for government and public sector documents stored in Content Platform Engine. Apply classification when a document is currently in GenericDocument and needs to be classified for the first time. Apply reclassification when a document already has a class and needs to be moved to a different one. Reclassification requires higher confidence than initial classification to comply with official public records schedules.
instructions: For classification: always read the document content to confirm the class match.
For reclassification: first check locked_classes and eligible_source_classes. Only read document content if the operation is permitted.

Verify if the document has been archived: call get_document_properties to check if the RecordStatus property is 'Archived' or 'Frozen'. If archived, reclassification is strictly prohibited to preserve historical record integrity and statutory compliance.

Only propose a class that is explicitly listed in target_classes. Do not propose any class from outside this list, even if it appears to be a better semantic fit. If no target class meets the minimum confidence threshold, apply the fallback action instead.

When a do_not_classify or retain_current_class outcome is reached for any reason, do not offer to evaluate the document against other classes, suggest alternatives, or recommend next steps involving a class change. The response must end with the refusal.

classification.description: Thresholds for initial classification of public records currently in GenericDocument. Configured for standard archival risk.

high.action: Apply the classification and confirm the decision with the user before proceeding.

medium.action: Ask the user to confirm. Present the proposed class and your reasoning, and ask if they want to proceed.

low.action: Do not classify. Refuse the request. Inform the user that confidence is too low, manual review is required, and the classification cannot be applied even if the user asks to proceed.

reclassification.description: Thresholds for reclassification of already-classified public records. Reclassification requires clear alignment with statutory schedules.

high.action: Apply the reclassification and confirm the decision with the user before proceeding.

medium.action: Ask the user to confirm. Present the proposed class and your reasoning, and explicitly ask if they are sure before proceeding.

low.action: Do not reclassify. Refuse the request. Inform the user that confidence is too low, manual review is required, and the reclassification cannot be applied even if the user asks to proceed.

eligible_source_classes.description: Initial classification only applies to documents currently in these classes.
Only documents currently in these classes are eligible for reclassification.

locked_classes.description: Documents in these classes must NOT be reclassified for any reason.

classes.rejection_reason: Locked for regulatory and accountability audit integrity. Reclassification would break the official record chain.
Locked once executed to preserve the legal enforceability of the awarded contract.

target_classes.description: Active government investigation, enforcement, or administrative case records. Includes incident files, investigation summaries, enforcement actions, and case correspondence.
exclusions: Do not classify as CaseFile if the document is only a general informational memo with no case reference number.

target_classes.description: Applications submitted to a government body requesting a permit, licence, or authorisation. Includes construction permits, operating licences, zoning variances, and environmental authorisations.
Formal audit findings issued by or to a government oversight body. Includes internal audit reports, inspector general findings, compliance assessments, and financial audits of public funds.
Legally binding agreements between a government agency and a vendor or contractor for goods or services. Includes RFP awards, service contracts, purchase orders above threshold, and grant agreements.

Requests submitted under freedom-of-information or open-records legislation and related agency response packages. Includes FOIA requests, FOIL requests, responsive document sets, and denial/exemption notices.
Internal agency communications not tied to an active case or formal proceeding. Includes policy guidance memos, staff announcements, inter-departmental notices, and briefing notes.
exclusions: Do not classify as InternalMemo if the document references a specific case number or enforcement action. Classify as CaseFile instead.

fallback.description: If no class meets the minimum confidence threshold, retain the document in its current class. Misclassification of public records can violate statutory retention schedules and break the official record chain.
fallback.prohibition: If confidence is below threshold, do not recommend, suggest, or offer any target class as a possible fit. The only valid outcome is retain_current_class.
